entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Maximilian Johannes Maria Hubert Reichsgraf von Spee was a German naval officer in the Imperial German Navy, who commanded the East Asia Squadron during World War I. Spee entered the navy in 1878 and served in a variety of roles and locations, including on a colonial gunboat in German West Africa in the 1880s, the East Africa Squadron in the late 1890s, and as commander of several warships in the main German fleet in the early 1900s. During his time in Germany in the late 1880s and early 1890s, he married his wife, Margareta, and had three children, his sons Heinrich and Otto and his daughter Huberta.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As commander of the East Asia Squadron during World War I, Spee played a significant role in the war's naval strategy, particularly in the Battle of the Falkland Islands. His actions led to increased British attention on German colonies and contributed to the eventual sinking of several British ships.
